evidence: Attribution claim (divergences are harness artifacts, not policy differences) is backed by four mechanistically-explained divergences in validation.tex sec val-scope: (1) live startup_time inverts offline semantics (immediate registration vs invisible-until-ready) — an option-semantics artifact; (2) capacity-model starvation traced to tracking-mode last-FPM-per-tick sampling (verified in /home/gio/tese/simulation/live51/planner_live_patch.py); (3) tick-cadence stretch under wall-clock stall vs offline virtual clock; (4) budget-unit mismatch (GPUs live vs replicas offline). Each is an implementation/harness property independent of the forecast-vs-reactive policy comparison. The one fix on a local branch (opt-in fpm_observation_mode) is real: planner_live_patch.py restores offline FPM-feed semantics. The chapter shows SLA verdicts agree on both policies (both graded metrics) and TTFT/replica-time within single digits, so divergences do not flip the policy verdict. Claim is scoped to 'the divergences that do exist' — appropriately hedged, not a universal no-policy-divergence claim.
